title: the mouth full of universe
carry: a little dirt on his lips

segments.voice: Last week ended with the butter thief dragging a mortar between two trees, and two cursed brothers walking free. Your line was two trees fall, two men go free.

Mother, Krishna ate dirt! The other boys come running to tell on him, his older brother Balarama among them. Small children put things in their mouths, and this one has just put a handful of earth in his. Yashoda grabs him by the hand, scolds him, and asks why. And the little boy, dirt on his lips, looks his mother in the eye and denies everything.

I didn't eat any dirt, Mother. They're lying. If you think they're telling the truth, look in my mouth yourself. So he opens it, and she looks in. And there, inside her son's mouth, she sees everything. The Bhagavata lists it as if it can hardly stop: the sky and the directions, the mountains, the islands and oceans, the whole round earth, wind and fire, the moon and the stars. The turning of time. The gods. The elements that make up a body, and the mind itself. And in among all of it, the village of Vraja, and in the village, herself. She's standing in her yard looking into her son's mouth, and inside it she finds her yard, and herself standing in it. The text doesn't let her off easily. She's frightened. Is this a dream? Is this an illusion sent by God? Is my own mind confused? Or is it some power that belongs to my child? She doesn't know what to call it. So she bows, inwardly, to the one beyond all thought, in whom all of this rests. Here is what the story is saying. The baby she nurses, the boy she ties to a mortar, the one who steals the neighbors' butter, holds everything that is. Not a picture of it. All of it, her included. And the doorway to that vision is a small boy's open mouth, with a little dirt on his lips.
screen: `"LOOK IN MY MOUTH."` · `SKY, MOUNTAINS, OCEANS, STARS.` · `THE VILLAGE, AND HERSELF IN IT.` · then, large: `A DREAM, OR GOD, OR MY CHILD?`

segments.voice: Start with what's closest, your breath, then widen: the room, the street, the town, the land and sea beyond, the sky over it all, and the stars past the sky. Hold that as wide as you can for a few breaths, then come back to your breath and notice that you're inside all of it, the way Yashoda saw herself inside the vision. If you pray, you can rest in prayer here.
Yashoda. Krishna's mother, who looks into her son's mouth for dirt, and finds everything, and herself.
Your line: a little dirt on his lips. Tomorrow, what she does with what she saw. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Krishna devotees tell this story alongside the butter-thief stories, and devotional paintings and songs show Yashoda peering into the child's open mouth.

Yashoda.meaning: Krishna's foster mother in the cowherd village

Vraja.meaning: the cowherd country where Krishna grows up
